answer: To deter Sybil attacks, an agent network can bind identities to radio multipath telemetry. A node proves physical presence by sounding a harbor with radar pulses, using an attestation kernel to verify backscatter from shoreline juniper stands. An attacker attempting to harbor fake nodes must deploy discrete transceivers at separate locations, incurring substantial hardware and siting costs. However, dense marine fog attenuates RF reflections, occasionally causing false rejections.
